questions.text: Which natural feature can 'blow its top' when magma erupts?
questions.explanation: A volcano erupts when molten rock, ash and gas escape from beneath the crust.

questions.text: What do we call a huge river of slowly moving ice?
questions.explanation: Glaciers form from compacted snow and flow downhill under their own weight.

questions.text: What name is given to a hot spring that erupts jets of steam and water, like Old Faithful?
questions.explanation: Geysers erupt when underground water is heated and forced upward.

questions.text: Which scale is used to rate the hardness of minerals?
questions.explanation: The Mohs scale ranks minerals from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond).

questions.text: Which mineral is the hardest on the Mohs scale?
questions.explanation: Diamond rates 10, the top of the Mohs scale.

questions.text: Which scale classifies wind force with terms such as 'gale' and 'storm'?
questions.explanation: The Beaufort scale runs from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane force).

questions.text: What is the layer of Earth lying between the crust and the core?
questions.explanation: The mantle makes up most of Earth's volume.

questions.text: Which type of rock, such as marble, forms when existing rock is changed by heat and pressure?
What name is given to the supercontinent that existed about 300 million years ago?
questions.explanation: Pangaea began to break up roughly 200 million years ago.

questions.text: Which cloud type, with an anvil-shaped top, is associated with thunderstorms?
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds are towering storm clouds that produce lightning and heavy rain.

questions.text: What is the term for the zone where one tectonic plate slides beneath another?
questions.explanation: Subduction zones produce deep ocean trenches and many volcanoes and earthquakes.

questions.text: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer chiefly found?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer sits in the stratosphere and absorbs much ultraviolet radiation.

questions.text: Which German scientist proposed the theory of continental drift in 1912?
questions.explanation: Wegener argued the continents had once been joined and had moved apart.

questions.text: Which 1883 volcanic eruption in Indonesia produced one of the loudest sounds in recorded history?
questions.explanation: The Krakatoa explosion was heard thousands of kilometres away.

questions.text: What is the boundary between Earth's crust and mantle called?
questions.explanation: The Moho was identified in 1909 by Andrija Mohorovičić from seismic waves.

spares.text: What is the name for balls of ice that fall from storm clouds?
spares.explanation: Hail forms in strong thunderstorm updrafts.

spares.text: Which mineral is the main component of sand on most inland and many coastal beaches?
spares.explanation: Quartz is a hard, chemically stable form of silica and survives weathering.

spares.text: What is the line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure on a weather map called?
spares.explanation: Isobars show pressure patterns and wind strength.

spares.text: Which type of volcano, like Mauna Loa, has broad, gently sloping sides built from runny lava?
spares.explanation: Shield volcanoes are built by fluid basaltic lava flows.
